title: About Pelham Services: domestic trucking
content:
Your freight. Los Angeles to Florida.

Pelham Services specializes in domestic Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) freight transport along the Los Angeles to Florida corridor. We pick up cargo directly from West Coast suppliers and manufacturers, delivering to retailers, distributors and logistics facilities across Florida, including freight forwarders and transit hubs in Miami.

Service boundary: Pelham Services provides specialized domestic over-the-road trucking. For export or cross-border shipments, our coverage concludes upon verified delivery to your designated forwarder, warehouse or international carrier terminal in Florida. We do not provide direct international ocean or air shipping, rail transport or port drayage services.

Capacity and handling around your shipment.

Choose LTL for shared trailer space or FTL for exclusive truck capacity. Cross-docking and palletizing support the movement of your freight.

Pelham operates facilities in Los Angeles, Orlando and Miami. Contact our team to confirm the appropriate receiving location and arrangements for your shipment.

[pelham_services]

For the businesses behind every pallet.

  • Suppliers and manufacturers: coordinate pickups directly from your Los Angeles facility to your Florida customers. Please provide total pallet counts, pallet dimensions (L × W × H), gross weight and cargo ready dates.
  • Distributors: streamline your inventory replenishment by sharing your receiving addresses, dock hours, appointment rules and any special site requirements so we can match your volume to the right service level.
  • Freight forwarders: secure domestic linehaul from Southern California to your Florida receiving terminal or export hub. Pelham Services handles the overland segment; our scope completes upon verified delivery at your designated domestic facility.

Before requesting a rate, review what to include in your freight quote. Need help selecting capacity? Compare LTL and FTL.

Business-to-business freight shipping

Pelham Services provides specialized domestic LTL freight transport connecting California suppliers and manufacturers with Florida distributors, retailers and freight forwarders. Whether you need high-volume pallet shipping or ongoing inventory replenishment, simply provide your shipping cadence, cargo details and receiving requirements. We handle the complete domestic linehaul move, providing a seamless handoff to your team before any onward international transit.

Explore LTL shipping for suppliers, manufacturers and distributors, or learn about delivery to Miami freight forwarders.

title: Freight technology: questions shippers should ask
content:
The short answer

Evaluate freight technology by whether it helps you make a shipping decision quickly and confidently: obtain a usable status update, keep shipment details consistent or coordinate receiving. Ask for the actual workflow, access requirements and limitations. A portal link alone does not establish live GPS tracking or automated alerts.

Visibility: what information will you actually receive?

Almost every carrier advertises advanced technology, but buzzwords do not move freight; clear communication does. “Tracking” also means different things: a single “dispatched” email is not the same as updates at each stage.

  • Which pickup, transit and delivery updates are available?
  • Are updates provided by a person, a portal or another channel?
  • Does a status describe the shipment or show a live vehicle position?
  • Which reference and contact should you use when an update is late or the receiver needs a new arrival estimate?

At Pelham: there is no live GPS tracking. The status is updated at each milestone: freight picked up, arrival at the origin warehouse, departure to Florida, arrival at the destination warehouse, delivery and proof of delivery.

Digital paperwork: can both sides use the same details?

Many billing adjustments come from differences between the purchase order, the packing list and the bill of lading (BOL). A useful digital process keeps cargo descriptions, dimensions, weight, addresses and dock instructions consistent. Ask how changes to dimensions, pallet count or delivery instructions are submitted after the quote, and which version governs the arrangement.

Pelham has a digital account application. It speeds up billing setup, but account submission does not itself reserve capacity or book a load.

Planning: does the information support the receiving deadline?

Software can plan routes, but it cannot override receiving appointments, traffic or loading delays. Ask which timing information is confirmed and which is estimated, and who coordinates appointment changes with a Florida distribution center or Miami forwarder. At Pelham, the customer service and dispatch team handles that coordination. Compare this with the actual destination and appointment requirement. Technology cannot turn a non-guaranteed transit estimate into a delivery guarantee.

A simple evaluation worksheet

These are evaluation questions, not claims that Pelham provides every feature or a ranking of current industry trends.

Apply the questions to your shipment

For an operational question, contact Pelham. For a new load, first prepare the shipment details, then request a quote. Choose based on confirmed service fit, lane experience and clear communication rather than a technology label or a software demo.

title: How Pelham plans a domestic freight shipment
content:
The short answer

Every Pelham shipment follows five steps:

  1. Enquiry: you share the shipment details.
  2. Review: Pelham’s customer service and dispatch team matches the load with LTL or FTL capacity.
  3. Confirmation: price, load details and pickup and receiving arrangements are confirmed.
  4. Handoff: pickup and receiving are coordinated.
  5. Follow-up: you receive status updates at each milestone, through to proof of delivery.

Sending a form or applying for an account does not itself book a shipment: it becomes active once the load details, price and pickup date are confirmed.

1. Give the team a usable enquiry

Accurate information avoids billing adjustments later. Share:

  • Pickup and receiving ZIP codes, with full business addresses when possible.
  • The ready date at pickup.
  • Goods and packaging: boxes, crates or drums.
  • Pallet count and loaded dimensions, including any overhang.
  • Total weight.
  • Appointment, liftgate or handling requirements.

Use the freight quote checklist to collect missing details from the supplier or receiver.

2. Discuss capacity and service

  • Shared LTL capacity: 1 to 7 pallets that can travel with other commercial freight. Choose Economy (estimated 10 days), Regular (7) or Expedited (3, Homestead–West Palm Beach only).
  • Exclusive FTL capacity: a 53’ trailer for 8 pallets or more (volume load or full truckload), heavy freight or cargo that should not share space. It can go directly from pickup to delivery, with one driver or a two-driver team, as you prefer.

If you are unsure, select “Help me choose” instead of selecting a service only by name. The LTL vs. FTL guide explains the difference; the LTL page lists transit estimates and coverage.

3. Confirm before treating the shipment as booked

  • Service and load details.
  • Quoted amount and included charges, such as the fuel surcharge and handling.
  • Pickup and receiving addresses, contacts and hours.
  • Required references (PO or BOL) and appointments.
  • Expected timing and any unresolved requirement.

Raise questions before dispatch. If a detail changes after the discussion, request confirmation of the revised plan.

4. Coordinate the handoff

  • California suppliers: have the cargo packed, labeled and ready on the dock before the agreed pickup window.
  • Florida receivers and Miami forwarders: provide the receiving references, such as a warehouse receipt or booking number, for the bill of lading.

Describe any palletizing or transfer needs in advance. For a Miami forwarder, the agreed delivery is domestic; the receiving guide explains how to separate the onward arrangement.

5. Keep the reference for updates

Pelham updates the shipment status at each milestone. It does not offer live GPS tracking:

  1. Freight picked up.
  2. Arrival at the origin warehouse.
  3. Departure to Florida.
  4. Arrival at the destination warehouse.
  5. Delivery.
  6. Proof of delivery.

Use the shipment reference whenever you contact the customer service and dispatch team for an update, a schedule change or delivery confirmation. For an existing shipment, contact Pelham with its reference. For a new load, start a freight enquiry. Account application, shipment enquiry and a confirmed transport arrangement are distinct steps.

title: Planning for freight delays and changes on a California–Florida shipment
content:
The short answer

If a freight plan changes, first identify the affected shipment and tell the carrier and receiving business what changed. Confirm the latest pickup or receiving arrangement before making further commitments. A transit estimate is not a guaranteed appointment; do not treat an unconfirmed arrival as a confirmed onward connection.

Why California–Florida freight plans change

Freight from Los Angeles to Florida travels about 2,700 miles over several days. Some 2,300 to 2,400 of them are on Interstate 10, the main route from Los Angeles to Tallahassee and Jacksonville; from there, trucks head south on I-75, I-95 or Florida’s Turnpike. Even with good planning, loading delays at a warehouse, severe weather, traffic and changing receiving appointments can affect the schedule. Fast, structured communication between the carrier, the supplier and the receiver keeps a small change from becoming a costly disruption.

If the shipment is already moving

  1. Find the reference: have the Pelham quote reference or the bill of lading (BOL) number ready.
  2. Check the latest status: Pelham updates each shipment at its milestones, from pickup to proof of delivery. Contact the customer service and dispatch team and ask what is confirmed and what remains estimated.
  3. Tell the receiving business: the Florida receiver can adjust dock staff or reschedule the appointment.
  4. Coordinate the next leg separately: if a Miami forwarder or another company handles the next leg, give it the revised arrival estimate so it can review its cut-off.

Rule: a transit estimate is an operational target, not a guaranteed appointment. Do not schedule an international departure or a production shift on an unconfirmed arrival.

Request an existing-shipment update. This guide does not promise a particular resolution, compensation or tracking feature.

If the load is not ready for pickup

  • Tell the team right away when the ready date, pallet count, dimensions or weight changes.
  • Reconfirm price and capacity: extra pallets or a new pickup day can change the space and the arrangement. Ask whether the quote still applies.
  • Get a realistic readiness date from the supplier, and check the receiver’s availability, before agreeing a new pickup.

If the receiving details change

If a Miami, Orlando or Jacksonville receiver changes the delivery location or dock hours, send the new street address, suite or door, receiving contact and appointment rules. Ask what the change means for the existing arrangement. For a forwarder, use the domestic receiving address in Florida, not the overseas destination, and coordinate any onward international schedule with that company.

Reduce avoidable uncertainty on the next shipment

  • Measure early: give loaded dimensions (length × width × height) and total weight rather than assuming standard pallet sizes.
  • Give both dates: the pickup ready date and the receiver’s actual deadline.
  • Name the contacts: who communicates changes at the supplier and at the receiving business.
  • Choose the right LTL level: match the urgency to Economy, Regular or Expedited, and review coverage and estimated timing before booking.

Use the right next step

For a shipment already arranged, contact the team with its reference. For a new load, use the quote preparation checklist and review LTL coverage before requesting service.

title: Full truckload shipping from California to Florida
content:
One truck. Your load.

Full truckload service reserves a 53’ trailer for one shipper. It suits a full load or freight that needs exclusive space, with pickup and delivery planned around your requirements.

Share your route, requested dates, dimensions, weight and equipment needs. For smaller loads that can share trailer space, explore our specialty: Less Than Truckload (LTL).

Questions before you ship

Must my shipment fill the trailer?

No. Exclusive trailer capacity may also suit freight that must travel separately. Discuss your load with our team.

Can I book a single shipment?

You can enquire about a one-time load or recurring work. Availability is confirmed when quoting.

Can my load travel with two drivers?

Yes. You choose one driver or a two-driver team. With two drivers, the truck keeps moving for longer and transit is shorter. A full truckload can go directly from pickup to delivery without passing through a terminal.

How are FTL rates set?

Rates are dynamic and change with the market, so each load is quoted for its dates. For recurring loads, contract rates are available: the agreed rate plus a fuel percentage that goes up or down with fuel prices.

Do the LTL transit levels apply to FTL?

No. Expedited, Regular and Economy are LTL service levels. FTL timing is discussed separately for your shipment.

Choosing between full truckload and a partial load?

For California–Florida freight, exclusive trailer capacity and shared LTL space solve different needs. Use our LTL vs. FTL guide to compare load size, handling and timing. If shared space fits, explore Los Angeles–Florida LTL shipping.

Full truckload from Los Angeles to Miami and Florida

For an FTL shipment from California to Florida, Pelham’s core pickup area is Los Angeles. Tell us the exact pickup and receiving addresses, including any Miami delivery requirements. A dedicated truck in this context means exclusive capacity for your shipment; discuss availability for each one-time or recurring move.

Requesting FTL rates. Include loaded dimensions, total weight, cargo, requested pickup date and receiving restrictions. The team confirms the quote and timing for your full truckload. The 3-, 7- and 10-day LTL estimates do not apply to FTL. Request a California–Florida full truckload quote.

title: LTL shipping from California to Florida
content:
Your pallets. Our specialty.

Ship 1 to 7 pallets without reserving an entire truck. Pelham collects your freight in Los Angeles and delivers it to businesses in Florida, including transport companies in Miami that may arrange a separate onward journey.

Our service is domestic trucking. We do not provide the international leg or direct port service. For exclusive trailer capacity, compare Full Truckload (FTL).

LTL freight from California to Florida

Pelham specializes in pallet shipping from Los Angeles to Florida. Share trailer space for shipments of 1 to 7 pallets; for 8 pallets or more, the team quotes a volume load or a full truckload. Provide the actual California pickup address when requesting a quote so our team can confirm arrangements for the origin, rather than assuming every California location has the same pickup plan.

Our Los Angeles facility is in Gardena. We deliver to Florida businesses, including shops, distributors and freight forwarders. Select a service level using the receiving address and timing needs, then request an LTL freight quote.

Pallet delivery across Florida

Los Angeles to Miami and South Florida. Pelham moves pallets to Miami businesses and transport companies. Expedited LTL estimates 3 calendar days from pickup and is limited to Homestead–West Palm Beach. Regular and Economy are also available for this area. For a forwarder, confirm the domestic receiving address and review our Miami delivery coordination guide.

Los Angeles to Orlando. Regular and Economy serve Orlando with estimated transit of 7 and 10 calendar days from pickup. Our Orlando facility is at 9777 Satellite Blvd suite 130. Confirm the shipment’s delivery address with the team; a business delivery and delivery to a Pelham facility are different arrangements.

Los Angeles to Tampa and Jacksonville. Regular and Economy serve these Florida destinations, with estimated transit of 7 and 10 calendar days from pickup. Supply the receiving business address and its requirements. Pelham does not list a company-operated facility in either city.

All transit times are estimates, not guarantees. Our operated facilities are in Gardena / Los Angeles, Miami and Orlando. Destination coverage is broader than our facility network.

Questions before you ship

When does the transit time start?

The estimate starts when your cargo is picked up and is counted in calendar days. Transit times are not guaranteed.

Where is Expedited available?

Expedited has an estimated transit time of 3 calendar days from pickup and serves South Florida from Homestead to West Palm Beach. Regular (7 days) and Economy (10 days) serve all Florida destinations.

Which option is the most economical?

Economy is our lowest-cost LTL service level, with an estimated transit time of 10 calendar days from pickup. Request a quote for your shipment.

Do you ship internationally?

No. Pelham provides domestic trucking. We can deliver to a transport company in Miami; any onward international movement is handled separately by that company.

How many pallets can ship LTL?

LTL covers shipments of 1 to 7 pallets. For 8 pallets or more, request a quote and the team will price a volume load or a full truckload.

What affects an LTL quote?

LTL is billed on the greater of the actual weight and the dimensional weight (length × width × height in inches ÷ 194). Share pallet or piece count, dimensions, total weight, cargo, pickup and delivery locations, receiving requirements and your preferred service level. The team confirms pricing for your shipment; no fixed rate is implied by a transit estimate.

For the businesses behind every pallet.

Suppliers and manufacturers: coordinate pallet pickup at your Los Angeles business or factory with the receiving business in Florida. Include loaded dimensions, weight and when the goods will be ready. Pallet shipping for suppliers starts with a clear description of the goods and packaging; acceptance and handling are confirmed for the shipment.

Distributors and wholesalers: plan California–Florida freight around replenishment and business receiving requirements. For recurring shipments, share your expected frequency and how pallet counts vary. Commercial freight delivery in Florida is arranged to the agreed business address; discuss each receiving location separately. See our recurring freight planning guide.

Freight forwarders: arrange the Los Angeles–Florida trucking leg and delivery to your receiving facility. Pelham’s service ends at the agreed domestic delivery point; onward international transport is handled separately.

title: Cross-docking, transloading and palletizing: which do you need?
content:
The short answer

Transloading describes transferring freight between transport equipment; cross-docking describes moving inbound freight into an outbound movement with limited storage. Palletizing prepares goods on pallets. You do not always have to pick one: a single shipment often uses all three. Describe the incoming load and desired outbound shipment rather than assuming only one label applies.

What each operation solves

Tip: loose boxes arriving in a container may be transloaded into a truck, palletized for safe handling and cross-docked onto an outbound Florida shipment. Storage duration, materials, timing and exact handling must be agreed for the shipment.

Describe the result you need

  • What is arriving: a container, trailer or box truck; floor-loaded, crated or already palletized; with cargo and packaging details.
  • Preparation needed: sorting, palletizing, shrink-wrapping, labeling or separation into different outbound loads.
  • Outbound details: the Florida destination, such as Miami, Orlando or Jacksonville, the receiving business and how the cargo should leave.
  • Timing and storage: an immediate dock-to-dock transfer or temporary staging before pickup, and any deadline. Ask which handling can be accommodated.

A container-to-truck scenario

Imported goods arrive at an agreed Los Angeles receiving facility and need to move by truck to a distribution center in Miami:

  1. Arrival: the goods arrive as loose boxes, floor-loaded in an ocean container.
  2. Palletizing: the boxes are unloaded, stacked on pallets and shrink-wrapped for domestic transport.
  3. Transloading and cross-docking: the pallets move across the dock into a truck bound for South Florida, without long-term storage.

This example does not imply Pelham collects at the port or handles customs.

What to confirm before dispatch

  • Appointments: receiving and pickup times at the transfer facility.
  • Materials: if palletizing is needed, the pallet size (for example, 48 × 40 in) and wrapping.
  • Charges: labor, pallet materials, handling and which services are included.
  • Outbound details: final pallet count and total weight, outbound capacity, receiving business and delivery requirements.

Discuss the handling arrangement

Use the container-transfer preparation checklist, then request a handling quote. Pelham offers cross-docking, transloading and palletizing for domestic trucking; international transport, rail and direct port service are outside its offer.

title: LTL vs. FTL: which fits your California–Florida shipment?
content:
The short answer

LTL means less than truckload: your freight shares trailer space. FTL means full truckload: you reserve exclusive trailer capacity. At Pelham, LTL covers 1 to 7 pallets; from 8 pallets, the team quotes a volume load or a full truckload. Dimensions, weight, handling and timing also affect the fit.

LTL vs. FTL at a glance

Tip: do not assume LTL is always cheaper. When a load gets close to 8 pallets or takes up a lot of trailer space, ask for both quotes: exclusive capacity can lower the cost per pallet. Compare written quotes for the same load and receiving requirements.

Which option fits your shipment?

Choose LTL if

  • You are shipping 1 to 7 pallets that do not need a whole trailer.
  • The cargo can travel safely alongside other commercial freight.
  • You can work with the LTL transit estimate for your destination.

Choose FTL if

  • You have 8 pallets or more, or the load reaches the trailer’s weight capacity.
  • The freight needs exclusive capacity: high-value or delicate goods, cargo that cannot be stacked or strict security requirements.
  • The load should go directly from pickup to delivery, without being consolidated with other shipments or passing through a terminal.
  • The deadline is tight: with a two-driver team, the truck keeps moving for longer and transit is shorter.

Not sure? Send measurements and weight, and select “Help me choose”. The team confirms whether the cargo, packaging and handling fit shared transport.

Two situations, two different questions

LTL: a Los Angeles supplier sends 2 pallets of boxed packaging to a warehouse in Miami. Shared LTL capacity is the natural fit.

FTL for a partial load: a shipper has 5 pallets of high-value electronics that cannot be stacked or mixed with other freight. The trailer will not be full, but exclusive FTL capacity keeps the load separate.

These examples illustrate the decision; they are not acceptance or price commitments.

How do Pelham transit options differ?

  • Expedited LTL: estimated 3 calendar days from pickup, for South Florida only, from Homestead to West Palm Beach.
  • Regular LTL: estimated 7 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations.
  • Economy LTL: estimated 10 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations. Pelham’s lowest-cost LTL level, suited to flexible replenishment.

All are estimates, not guarantees. FTL timing is quoted separately for each shipment and depends on whether you choose one driver or a two-driver team. See current LTL coverage and service levels.

How should you compare LTL and FTL rates?

  • Give both enquiries the same pickup and delivery ZIP codes, cargo, dimensions, total weight and ready date.
  • Confirm which additional services are included, such as a liftgate or an appointment.
  • Rates are dynamic and change with the market: compare quotes requested at the same time.
  • Compare the total quoted amount against the volume shipped, and the timing, rather than assuming a fixed saving for LTL.

For a partial shipment, the pallet shipping cost guide explains which details affect the quote.

Choose capacity or ask the team to help

Explore LTL shared capacity or FTL exclusive capacity. If the choice is still unclear, request a quote and select “Help me choose”. The team confirms the arrangement before booking.

title: Freight quote requirements: what to prepare
content:
The short answer

To request a useful freight quote, provide pickup and delivery locations, goods and packaging, pallet count, loaded dimensions, weight and a ready date. Add the service preference and receiving requirements if known. State units and distinguish weight per pallet from total shipment weight.

Freight quote checklist

Missing dimensions or a vague delivery address slow a quote down. Giving these details upfront gets you a more accurate rate on the first try and avoids adjustments later:

  • Pickup: business name, city/state/ZIP, contact and the date the goods will be ready.
  • Delivery: receiving business, city/state/ZIP and any access instructions, such as restricted access, appointments or limited hours; include street addresses when available. Say whether the receiver needs a liftgate. Pelham delivers to businesses; if you are already a customer and an occasional shipment goes to a home address, tell the team.
  • Goods: what is being shipped (for example, printed packaging or machinery parts), how it is packed (pallets, crates or loose boxes) and the pallet or piece count.
  • Measurements: length × width × height of each pallet after it is loaded and wrapped, including any overhang, for each size group; specify inches or other units.
  • Weight: weight per pallet and total shipment weight, with units. Pelham bills the greater of the actual weight and the dimensional weight, so use scale weights rather than guesses.
  • Service: LTL level, FTL or “Help me choose”; identify any palletizing or transfer need.

A message you can copy and complete

Pickup business and city/state/ZIP: [details]
Receiving business and city/state/ZIP: [details]
Ready date: [date]
Required delivery date: [date]
Goods and packaging: [description]
Pallet count: [count]
Loaded dimensions per size group: [length × width × height, units]
Weight per pallet and total: [values, units]
Service preference: [LTL level / FTL / help me choose]
Receiving or handling requirements: [details]

What if some information is missing?

Mark unknown details as unknown and ask the supplier or receiver to confirm them. You can start an enquiry with the information available to get an initial budget; the price is confirmed once measurements and weights are confirmed. Do not present estimates as measured values: a scale ticket avoids weight corrections later.

Three errors that create avoidable follow-up

1. Writing “two pallets” without dimensions or weight

Pallets come in different sizes. A standard 48 × 40 in pallet takes up different trailer space than an oversized 96 × 48 in one, so the team cannot calculate space or price without loaded dimensions and weight.

2. Giving the overseas destination for a Miami forwarder

If the goods are going to South America but Pelham picks them up in Los Angeles and delivers them to an export forwarder in Miami, give the Miami warehouse address. The quote covers where Pelham delivers.

3. Giving a deadline without a ready date

“It must arrive by Friday” is not enough if the team does not know when the goods will be packed. Give the ready date at pickup and the required delivery date, with the receiver’s appointment requirements.

Check the response before booking

  • Is the service correct: LTL level or FTL?
  • Which charges are included, such as fuel, a liftgate or an appointment?
  • Do the pickup and delivery addresses match your bill of lading (BOL)?
  • Are the pickup arrangements and expected timing clear?

An enquiry is not a booking. If the load, ready date or receiving details change, ask whether the quote still applies. Understand the pricing factors if you need to compare alternatives.

Send the completed details

Request your freight quote. For help choosing capacity, read LTL vs. FTL; for a Miami transport-company receiver, use the forwarder handoff guide.

title: Planning recurring California–Florida freight shipments
content:
The short answer

Plan recurring freight around a typical load, its expected variation, pickup readiness and the receiver’s availability. Recurring does not automatically mean FTL or a reserved pickup slot. Share the pattern with Pelham and confirm capacity, pricing and how changes will be handled.

Describe the normal pattern and the exceptions

Whether you move two pallets every week or several truckloads a month, volumes change with production, dock availability and seasonal peaks. A brief with the typical load and its expected variation lets the team confirm capacity and pricing and handle exceptions. Include these five details:

  1. Origin and destination: the usual pickup warehouse in California and receiving business in Florida.
  2. Frequency and ready days: how often you ship (for example, every Thursday morning) and when the goods are packed and ready.
  3. Typical load: pallet count, loaded dimensions (length × width × height), weight and goods.
  4. Variation and seasonality: peak periods, changing destinations or months when volume doubles or drops.
  5. Receiving requirements: appointment windows, dock access and the person coordinating each end.

A useful recurring shipment brief

“We expect [frequency] shipments from [supplier/location] to [receiver/location]. A typical load is [count, sizes, weight]. During [period] it may change to [variation]. Goods are normally ready [schedule], and the receiver requires [arrangements].” This is a planning brief, not a capacity reservation.

Choose capacity from the load, not the frequency

A common misconception is that recurring shipments always need a full truckload. The load decides:

  • Recurring LTL: steady partial loads of 1 to 7 pallets per shipment that can share trailer space.
  • Recurring FTL: 8 pallets or more per shipment (volume load or full truckload), or loads that need exclusive capacity in a 53’ trailer, with one driver or a two-driver team.

Tip: if volume peaks in certain months, ask about LTL for the normal months and a volume load or FTL for the peak season. See the capacity comparison rather than assuming all repeated shipments need dedicated trucks.

Agree what needs reconfirmation

Even on a regular schedule, tell the team about these changes before pickup. Keep the latest agreed details together.

How are recurring shipments priced?

Freight rates are dynamic and change with the market, so a previous quote does not automatically fix future prices or availability. For regular volumes, Pelham offers contract rates. A contract rate keeps the agreed base rate and adds a fuel percentage that goes up or down with fuel prices. Share the brief above and ask the team for a contract rate proposal.

Match the schedule to an LTL service level

  • Expedited LTL: estimated 3 calendar days from pickup, for South Florida only, from Homestead to West Palm Beach.
  • Regular LTL: estimated 7 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations.
  • Economy LTL: estimated 10 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations, suited to predictable, non-urgent replenishment.

These are estimates, not guarantees; plan the receiver’s stock with that margin.

Request a review of the pattern

Send a recurring freight enquiry using the brief above. Add the measurements and shipment details needed for the initial load. Confirm each arrangement before treating it as booked.

title: Understanding fuel surcharges in a freight quote
content:
The short answer

A fuel surcharge (FSC) is a freight pricing component that adjusts for changes in diesel prices, so the base rate can stay stable. To understand yours, identify the calculation basis, applicable rate or amount, effective period and whether it is already included in the quoted total. There is no universal percentage, and this guide does not publish Pelham’s current rate.

How the calculation works

Fuel surcharges vary by carrier and lane. Most quotes use one of two methods:

1. Percentage method

The most common: eligible base charge × applicable surcharge percentage = fuel charge. First confirm what the “eligible base” includes; it is often the linehaul charge only, without additional services.

2. Fixed amount or per-mile method

Some carriers, especially for full truckload, use a stated amount or a per-mile surcharge linked to a diesel price index. Follow the quote’s agreed basis rather than applying a percentage from elsewhere.

At Pelham: contract rates add a fuel percentage that goes up or down with fuel prices. Ask the team which percentage applies to your account or quote.

This explains the arithmetic, not a published Pelham rate.

Four questions that resolve most confusion

  1. Is fuel included? Is the quoted price all-in, or will a fuel surcharge be added to the invoice?
  2. What is the base? Which charge or quantity is the surcharge calculated on?
  3. Which date applies? Surcharges are often updated weekly or monthly: is the rate set by the booking date, the ready date or another date?
  4. How long is the quote valid? Fuel prices move quickly; check how long the rate applies.

Avoid counting fuel twice

An all-in quote may already include fuel. A base transport figure may list it separately.

Common mistake: adding a fuel percentage to an all-in total because you assumed fuel was not included.

Better practice: compare the final total of each quote, not the base rates alone, and identify included components and any conditional charges. Do not add a separate fuel amount to an all-in total unless the quote instructs you to do so.

Why an old percentage may not apply

A fuel surcharge is not a government tax or a single rate shared by every trucking company. It changes with current diesel prices, often measured by a published index such as the U.S. Department of Energy’s weekly diesel average, and with each carrier’s lane and operating costs. A historic screenshot, a six-month-old quote or another carrier’s fuel table does not establish the amount applicable to your shipment. Confirm the basis and validity with the team. If the route, date or load changes, ask whether the existing quote remains valid.

Clarify your quote before booking

For an existing quote, contact Pelham with its reference and ask for the calculation basis and included total. For a new shipment, request a freight quote. The pallet cost guide explains the other shipment details needed for pricing.

title: Preparing a container-to-truck transfer with Pelham
content:
The short answer

Before a container-to-truck transfer, align four things: who delivers the inbound container and its facility appointment, how the cargo is packed (floor-loaded or palletized), the handling required (sorting, palletizing, wrapping) and the outbound trucking plan. Ask Pelham which documents and approvals apply to that arrangement. There is no single universal document list, and this is not a port or customs checklist.

Prepare an information pack

A container that reaches a facility without preparation can cause container charges, dock congestion or handling delays. Assemble these details before scheduling its delivery:

Tip: if the container arrives floor-loaded, with loose boxes stacked to the roof, share the sender’s packing list upfront so the labor and pallet materials can be planned. The team must confirm the actual documents and receiving requirements; listing a document here does not make it mandatory for every shipment.

Confirm who is responsible before the facility

  • Your drayage or port carrier: delivers the container from the port or rail ramp to the agreed facility.
  • The transfer: unloading, inspection, palletizing if needed and staging at the agreed facility, as confirmed in the quote.
  • Pelham: the domestic trucking from California to the Florida receiver.

Pelham does not provide direct port service, international transport or customs clearance. Do not dispatch a container based only on a facility address listed online.

Describe how the cargo should leave

  • Shared LTL space: when the container’s contents are split among several Florida receivers.
  • Exclusive FTL capacity: when the whole load goes in a 53’ trailer to one receiver in Miami, Orlando or Jacksonville, directly and with one or two drivers.

Describe any palletizing need. Handling and transfer timing are confirmed separately from trucking transit estimates.

Before dispatching the inbound load

  • Appointment: confirm the receiving location, contact and appointment time for the inbound container.
  • Handling: confirm acceptance of the goods and the agreed sorting, palletizing or labeling.
  • References: make sure the outbound bill of lading (BOL) carries the required customer reference or purchase order (PO) numbers, and confirm the documentation for this arrangement.
  • Charges: agree labor, pallet materials, trucking, included services and timing.
  • Changes: if port delays or drayage holds move the arrival, tell the facility and Pelham immediately.

Send the transfer details for review

Discuss a container-to-truck transfer. If you are unsure which handling term applies, read transloading vs. cross-docking. Describe the actual task; the team confirms the arrangement.

title: How much does it cost to ship a pallet from California to Florida?
excerpt: Learn what affects the cost to ship one or more pallets from California to Florida, including Los Angeles to Miami, and prepare an accurate quote request.
content:
The short answer

There is no published fixed Pelham price for shipping one pallet from California to Florida. Pelham prices LTL shipments of 1 to 7 pallets on the greater of the actual weight and the dimensional weight (length × width × height in inches ÷ 194), plus the route, service level and receiving requirements. Request a shipment-specific quote for an actual amount.

What changes the cost of one pallet to Miami?

In freight, “one pallet” is not a standard unit of space or weight. These details drive a California–Florida pallet quote:

Tip: do not multiply an assumed single-pallet rate to estimate a larger load. Four pallets on one shipment are quoted as one shipment, not as four separate pallets. For several pallets, list each size and weight group. LTL covers 1 to 7 pallets; for 8 or more, ask for a volume load or full truckload quote. Sending, transporting and delivering the pallet are parts of the same shipment enquiry here; confirm the quote’s actual scope.

How is the billable weight of a pallet calculated?

Pelham does not use NMFC freight classes. A pallet is billed on whichever is greater: its actual weight or its dimensional weight. Dimensional weight reflects the trailer space the pallet takes up: multiply length × width × height in inches and divide by 194 to get pounds.

Example: a 48 × 40 × 60 in pallet measures 115,200 cubic inches. Divided by 194, its dimensional weight is about 594 lb. If the pallet actually weighs 400 lb, it is billed as 594 lb; if it weighs 900 lb, it is billed as 900 lb. A light, bulky pallet uses as much space as a heavy one, and the formula covers that space.

Why two one-pallet enquiries can differ

Consider a light, 3-foot stack of boxed goods and a 7-foot pallet of heavy machinery that cannot be stacked. Both are “one pallet,” but their loaded measurements, weight and use of space differ. Provide both sets of details to obtain comparable quotes. This example explains the inputs; it does not establish a price difference or acceptance.

Which service should you price?

Choose the level that balances your budget with the delivery deadline:

  • Economy LTL: Pelham’s lowest-cost level. Estimated 10 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations; suited to flexible replenishment.
  • Regular LTL: estimated 7 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations.
  • Expedited LTL: estimated 3 calendar days from pickup, for South Florida only, from Homestead to West Palm Beach.

These times are not guaranteed. Choose by actual destination and schedule, then compare the quoted total. Check LTL service coverage.

Before deciding that one quote is cheaper

  • Fuel: does the amount include the applicable fuel component, or will it be added later?
  • Scope: does the quote cover the whole domestic trip? Separate it from any onward international journey arranged by a Miami forwarder.
  • Additional services: is a liftgate or an appointment included?
  • Same specifications: keep the cargo, route, ready date, weight and stackability the same in both quotes.
  • Validity: rates are dynamic and change with the market. Check how long the quote applies and what changes would require a revised quote.

If the quote lists a fuel surcharge, use the fuel surcharge explanation to understand the calculation basis.

Get a price for your actual load

Have these six details ready:

  1. Pickup and delivery city/state/ZIP.
  2. Total pallet count.
  3. Loaded dimensions of each pallet (length × width × height).
  4. Total weight.
  5. Cargo description and packaging, stackable or not.
  6. Ready date.

Use the quote checklist if a supplier holds those details, then request pallet shipping rates. If exclusive trailer capacity is required, compare LTL with FTL first. Delivering to an export company? Read the Miami forwarder handoff guide.

title: Delivering California freight to a forwarder in Miami
excerpt: Arrange domestic LTL trucking from Los Angeles to a Miami freight forwarder. Prepare pallet details, receiving instructions and a separate onward shipment.
content:
The short answer

Use the Miami freight forwarder’s domestic receiving address for Pelham’s trucking quote, not the overseas destination. Confirm the receiver’s contact, reference and delivery requirements. Pelham moves the freight by truck from Los Angeles to the agreed receiver; the forwarder’s onward international arrangement is separate.

Who handles each part of the journey?

California freight bound for Latin America, the Caribbean or Europe often travels by truck to a forwarder in Miami or elsewhere in Florida. Knowing where the domestic trucking ends and the forwarder’s work begins avoids missed sailings, storage charges and misdirected cargo.

LTL services for freight forwarders mean shared domestic truck capacity in this context. Pelham does not provide international forwarding, rail transport, direct port service or customs clearance.

Ask the receiver these questions first

  1. Receiving address: what business name, street address, suite or door should appear on the trucking request?
  2. Hours and appointments: is an appointment needed, or does the dock receive during open hours? Who handles receiving, and how can they be contacted?
  3. References: which booking number, warehouse receipt or customer ID must appear on the bill of lading (BOL)?
  4. Onward deadline: what is the cargo cut-off for the planned vessel or flight?
  5. Receiving instructions: are specific pallet dimensions, labels, documents or unloading equipment required?

Example: a supplier delivering to a Miami forwarder

A Los Angeles supplier prepares 4 pallets that will eventually sail to Cartagena, Colombia.

Common mistake: entering “Cartagena, Colombia” as the delivery destination on the domestic freight request.

Correct approach: give the supplier’s Los Angeles pickup address as the origin and the Miami forwarder’s receiving address and ZIP code as the destination.

Coordinate the overseas destination, sailing and customs arrangements separately with the forwarder. A future international journey does not change the domestic delivery address.

How to handle an onward deadline

Missing an ocean or air cut-off can delay cargo by days or weeks. Share the target cut-off with Pelham before booking, so the team can recommend a service level, and ask the forwarder how changes affect its onward plan.

  • Expedited LTL: estimated 3 calendar days from pickup, for South Florida only, from Homestead to West Palm Beach. Useful for tight export cut-offs.
  • Regular LTL: estimated 7 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations.
  • Economy LTL: estimated 10 calendar days from pickup to all Florida destinations, for flexible, non-urgent transfers.

None is guaranteed. A transit estimate does not confirm an overseas departure.

Check the handoff before pickup

  • Reconcile pallet count, loaded height and dimensions, weight and goods with the quote.
  • Make sure the forwarder’s booking or warehouse reference appears on the pallets and the BOL.
  • Tell Pelham before dispatch if the receiver needs a liftgate, palletizing or transfer; these services are quoted with the shipment.
  • Ask the forwarder whether it needs the proof of delivery: Pelham sends it when the delivery is complete.
  • If the ready date, load or receiving arrangement changes, notify Pelham and the forwarder immediately.

Arrange the domestic leg

Review Los Angeles–Florida LTL service and request the domestic trucking quote. To estimate a pallet, read how much it costs to ship a pallet from California to Florida; for larger loads, compare LTL and FTL. For repeated shipments, the recurring freight guide helps structure the schedule.
